thread:
maria: ran a fresh kv-cache bench across regions + GPU families, posting quick summary + raw CSV. focus: paging behavior and hitrate vs p99 for mixed seqlen (short/mid/tail). results surprised me.
ajay: awesome, drop the CSV link? :eyes:
maria: https://internal.s3/redwood/kvbench/2154321987-results.csv (perf-bot also uploaded charts)
perf-bot: uploaded charts: /charts/2154321987/h100-a100-eu-us-apac.png
cheng: skimmed charts — A100 has slightly better tail when hitrate > 85%, H100 wins when hitrate drops below ~60% because kernel prefetch/pipeline wins.
lena: what quant levels did you use? int8 or int4?
maria: quant = int8 fastpath for model weights, kv values left fp16. also ran a int4 variant for two runs, results in sheet. int4 reduced mem pressure but added ~3-6% quality diff on our eval prompts.
devon: can you paste the bench command you ran?
maria: sure:
```
./bench_kvcache --model rdx-13b --gpus h100,a100 --regions us,eu,apac --slen_dist mixed_tail --quant int8 --duration 10m --prefetch_window 32 --evict_policy lru_threshold=0.6
```
ajay: nice. what was the effective cache hitrate curve across seqlen buckets?
maria: short(<=32): 94% hit, mid(33-256): 74% hit, tail(>256): 28% hit. p99 latency correlated strongly with tail hitrate.
cheng: did you observe KV spillback/paging events? numbers?
maria: yes — US H100: spillbacks 0.6% of requests, EU A100: 1.8%, APAC mixed: 2.4%. most spillbacks were during 95-99th percentile long sequences.
lena: any kernel fallback artifacts in the logs? e.g., switching from fused-attn to fallback kernel under certain seqlen?
maria: saw a few kernel switches logged around sequences >1024 where fused kernels refused due to memory fragmentation. attached log snippet.
perf-bot: log snippet uploaded: /logs/2154321987/kernel-switch.txt
devon: from a capacity planning POV, what's the effective throughput per GPU at 99% SLO?
maria: with current config: H100 ~ 650 tokens/s under mixed_tail at p99 SLO, A100 ~ 520 tokens/s. int4 bumped H100 to ~780 tokens/s but with the noted quality delta.
ajay: tradeoff clear. Could we get a hybrid: int8 for weights + cached kv int4? did you try that?
maria: not yet. plan to try kv-int4 with weight-int8 next week. open to suggestions on prefetch_window and eviction watermark.
cheng: try increasing prefetch_window to 64 for H100 only, reduces miss latency but increases mem usage; combine with raising evict_threshold to 0.7 so we keep warmer entries. also experiment with adaptive eviction: evict entries with low future-prob score.
lena: curious about regional kernel selection — do we route to A100 for long-tail-heavy jobs in EU by policy?
maria: in this bench we used uniform routing. separate run where routing policy picks A100 for long-tail reduced EU p99 by ~12% but reduced overall throughput due to A100 lower peak.
devon: for SLA talk with infra — what's a safe commit for Dedicated sizing? e.g., 100k reqs/day with our traffic mix -> how many H100s?
cheng: rough calc: use per-GPU throughput * duty cycle. For mixed_tail 100k reqs/day at avg tokens 120 -> ~12M tokens/day. H100 at 650 tokens/s is ~56M tokens/day (1 gpu full). but tail spikes matter, aim for 30% headroom -> 2 GPUs.
maria: added a note in the spreadsheet: /spreadsheets/kv-capacity-2154321987.
ajay: quality regressions — any eval diffs on the eval set with int8/4 runs? metric delta?
maria: int8: BLEURT delta -0.4, int4: -2.1 on our 1k eval set. specific failure modes: hallucination increase on long instruction chains.
lena: ok, push int8 to canary but hold int4 behind experiments unless we have mitigations (prompt-level constraints or rerank).
devon: ops ask: any config changes that require rollout controls? e.g., kernel toggles?
cheng: yes — kernel selections & prefetch window should be rollout controlled. add canary route with fallback to baseline if tail p99 increases by >10%.
maria: creating canary in prod staging tomorrow, will post results here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ajay: thanks — ping me when you need perf infra to run extended 24h run.
perf-bot: benchmark summary CSV, charts, and logs archived: /artifacts/kvbench/2154321987.zip
